module_title: Extremist Phase (1905-1918) - Policies, Pacts, and Reforms
introduction: At this level, we study the Extremists' working methods (National Education, Passive Resistance), the British 'Divide and Rule' policy implemented through the Morley-Minto Reforms, and crucial political realignments like the Lucknow Pact of 1916.

core_concepts.title: Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)
core_concepts.description: Also known as the Indian Councils Act 1909. It introduced the system of 'Separate Electorates' for Muslims, sowing the official seeds of communalism and the eventual partition of India.

core_concepts.title: Delhi Durbar and Annulment of Partition (1911)
core_concepts.description: A grand Durbar was held in Delhi to welcome King George V. Here, the Partition of Bengal was annulled, and it was announced that the capital would be shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

core_concepts.title: Lucknow Pact (1916)
core_concepts.description: Two major events occurred at the Lucknow session: 1) Moderates and Extremists reunited. 2) The Congress and Muslim League signed the Lucknow Pact, where Congress controversially accepted the League's demand for separate electorates.

core_concepts.title: National Education and Self-Reliance
core_concepts.description: During the Swadeshi movement, British educational institutions were boycotted. The 'National Council of Education' was set up in 1906 under Satish Chandra Mukherjee to promote indigenous learning.

important_entities.name: Aurobindo Ghosh
important_entities.significance: He propounded the theory of 'Passive Resistance' and edited the journal 'Vande Mataram'. He later retired from politics and moved to Puducherry.

important_entities.name: Lord Minto
important_entities.significance: Legalized communalism in India by creating separate constituencies for Muslims through the 1909 reforms.

important_entities.name: Ambika Charan Majumdar
important_entities.significance: Presided over the historic Lucknow Session where the Extremists were readmitted into the Congress.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Muslim League was formed in Dhaka in 1906 with British encouragement, primarily to counter the growing influence of the Congress and promote Muslim loyalty to the British.
The shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi was *announced* in 1911, but Delhi officially became the capital in 1912.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Maratha in English, Kesari in Marathi
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Students often mix these up. The newspaper named 'Maratha' was actually published in English, while 'Kesari' was in Marathi.

exam_strategy_tips: The introduction of 'Separate Electorates' in the 1909 Act is one of the most frequently asked questions in modern history.
Be clear on who reunited/signed pacts in 1916 (Extremists reunited with Moderates; Congress signed a pact with the Muslim League).
